scenes.title: Late payments cost freelancers time
scenes.body: Freelancers billing $5k-$30k a month chase invoices by hand.
scenes.caption: Freelancers lose money and time to late payments and awkward follow-up emails.

scenes.title: Step 1 · Upload the signed proposal
scenes.body: Drop in the signed PDF. InvoicePilot reads the payment schedule.
scenes.caption: First, I upload the signed proposal. InvoicePilot reads the agreed payment schedule.

scenes.title: Step 2 · Invoices on the agreed schedule
scenes.body: 3 invoices created: 40% deposit, 30% at midpoint, 30% on delivery.
scenes.caption: It creates the invoices on the schedule from the proposal: deposit, midpoint and delivery.

scenes.title: Step 3 · Polite reminders until paid
scenes.body: Reminder 1 at due date, then +3 and +7 days. Stops when paid.
scenes.caption: Polite reminders go out until the client pays, and they stop as soon as payment lands.

scenes.title: Connects to Stripe and QuickBooks
scenes.body: Payments reconcile automatically. No double entry.
scenes.caption: It connects to Stripe and QuickBooks, so payments reconcile without double entry.

experiment.hypothesis: Leading with the objection ("Will reminders annoy my clients?") gets more invoice schedules created per click than leading with the hook.
experiment.change: Swap the day-1 LinkedIn post to the Objection clip; keep copy, link and time the same.
experiment.metric: Invoice schedules created per tracked click
experiment.minimumSample: At least 100 tracked clicks per variant before choosing a winner
experiment.why: In the example data the Objection clip had the highest actions per click (6 of 38), but the sample is too small to call a winner.
